headline: 10y 5.041%, highest since 2007, hike odds 92% into FOMC Sep 16, Brent $107.55 +1.8%
stance: S&P futures -0.5% against an 8bp move in tens. The hike is priced for Sep 16; the projections are not.

news.head: 10-year tops 5%, highest since 2007
news.body: +8bp overnight, only the third intraday break of 5% since 2007. 30y 5.384%, 2y 4.686%.

news.head: Hike odds 92% for Wednesday
news.body: 25bp from the 3.50-3.75% range, up from 86% Monday. It would be the first Fed increase since July 2023.

news.head: Brent $107.55 with the Saudi pipeline still shut
news.body: Brent +1.8%, WTI $103.36, +2% (~6am ET). Riyadh has not said when the East-West line reopens.

news.head: Corning sells stock into the AI drawdown
news.body: Corning -12% Monday on a $2bn at-the-market offering announced after Friday's close. Coherent -11%, Lumentum -9%.

implications: A hike into a 5% 10-year tightens twice. The long end is repricing term premium, which the decision tomorrow does not fix.
Rate vol has risen four straight sessions and equity vol has not followed. Equity hedges stay cheap only while the repricing stays in the bond market.

watch.head: Empire State, today 8:30
watch.body: First regional manufacturing read of the month, and the last hard data before the Fed decides.

watch.head: FOMC, Sep 16, 2:00pm
watch.body: Projections and the dot plot at 2:00, Powell at 2:30. A hike at 92% is not the question; the 2027 path is.

watch.head: Retail sales, Sep 16, 8:30
watch.body: Lands six hours before the decision. It is a nominal series, so higher pump prices lift it. The control group is the read.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Monday's break of 5% on the 10-year reversed into the close. Overnight it held.
The front end led all week: 2y +22bp Wednesday to Monday. Overnight the 10y led instead, +8bp against the 2y's +5bp.
30y 5.384% overnight, above Monday's close. The long end is joining a selloff the front end has run alone since Wednesday.
sections.positioning: Gold specs at the 97th percentile, up 5 points on the week, a sixth week extended long. Real yields are setting the price, not the supply shock.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P futures -0.49%, Nasdaq-100 futures -0.48% (~6am ET). The bond move is not being paid for in equities yet.
Corning -12% Monday, Coherent -11%, Lumentum -9%, all on the same $2bn equity raise from an AI-infrastructure supplier.
Nvidia closed -3.4% Monday. The AI supply chain is issuing equity into the drawdown now, not buying it back.
sections.positioning: Russell 2000 specs sit at the 2nd percentile, a twentieth week extended short. Standing background into a hike, not a new signal.

single_name.note: Community Financial System: new on Monday's scan, an insider buy filed Sep 10. Holds its 200-day, 11.0 days to cover.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Commercial paper is where the oil move shows in funding costs, not in corporate spreads.
Investment grade and high yield both tightened into Friday's mark. Neither has repriced for a 5% 10-year.
Reverse repo is effectively empty. With the Treasury account drawing down, bank reserves are the only cushion left into a hike.
sections.positioning: Primary dealers hold investment-grade inventory at the 37th percentile of three years, mid-range. No inventory pressure either way into the decision.

ideas.line: 6 open · 0 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
